heading: INT. FERRY TICKET BOOTH, DESERTED PIER - DUSK

units.text: INT. FERRY TICKET BOOTH, DESERTED PIER - DUSK
A glass box no bigger than a phone booth, its paint flaking in sheets.
Fog presses at the windows.
ODALYS PRIETO, seventies, wrapped in a green cardigan, sits on a stool amid cardboard boxes marked in marker: LAST DAY.
On the counter, a battered cassette recorder with a masking-tape label.
She hesitates, then presses PLAY.
A hiss.
A younger woman's voice, warm and slightly breathless, fills the booth.
Test, test. Okay. This is Odalys, and it's the first of June, and the little ones are asleep, so I will whisper the schedule.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Odalys closes her eyes.
Her hand drifts across the counter and rests on a brass stamp.
Seven a.m., the fishermen. Eight, the schoolchildren, mind the puddles. Noon, nobody. Nobody ever, and that's when I read.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: The tape hisses.
Outside, a gull drops onto the pier rail and watches her.
If anyone ever hears this, I want you to know it was a good job. The best view in the county, and nobody to talk to but the tide.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Odalys smiles, then stops smiling.
She slides the stamp into her cardigan pocket, switches off the lamp, and presses STOP.
The silence rings.
It was.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: She pulls the shutter down.
